source_location: [low, high] NITI Overview Chapter 4, Green Hydrogen, text below Figure 4.7, p. 55 (PDF p. 101): CPS about 470 TWh and NZS 1,392 TWh in 2050; repeated as 470 and 1,400 TWh in Section 4.3, p. 59 (PDF p. 105) | [central] TERI Section 3.2.6 Hydrogen, p. 41 (PDF p. 58): around 896 TWh to produce 20 Mt in the Low Carbon scenario
notes: no: India's hydrogen today, about 6 Mt a year, is grey hydrogen made from fossil fuels (TERI p. 40), and NITI starts green hydrogen from a near-zero baseline (Overview p. 54), so electrolysis load is absent from the historical generation series. Grid caveat: TERI assumes this electricity comes from off-grid renewable plants and leaves it out of grid demand (p. 41); electricity supplied off-grid or by captive plants would not appear in NPP utility generation. central is the median of the three published 2050 figures. Implied electricity per kg, as a check on the published TWh: NITI 470 TWh for 8 Mt (CPS) and 1,392 TWh for 25 Mt (NZS) in 2050 (Overview Figure 4.7, p. 55) give 59 and 56 kWh/kg; with the Power volume's 8.5 Mt (CPS, Vol. 7 p. 32) and about 26 Mt (NZS, p. 33) they give 55 and 54 kWh/kg; TERI 896 TWh for 20 Mt gives 45 kWh/kg. Context: the National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 Mt a year by 2030 (NITI Power Vol. 7 p. 32, PDF p. 62, https://niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-02/Scenarios-Towards-Viksit-Bharat-and-Net-Zero-Sectoral-Insights-Power.pdf).
